steps.name: The readability check
steps.summary: A new script, scripts/readability.py, checks every line a diff adds against the six readable-code rules and names the file, line and rule for each problem.
changes: Tests: one case for each rule refusing a bad line and passing a good one, plus quoted text, HTML, table rows and names that already existed.
The readability check itself: it reads a diff, works out which lines are Python or JavaScript, and checks each added line against the six rules.

What I have proven, and what I have not
Tested in scratch copies of the repo; nothing is in the plugin yet.

Proven: the full suite passes 1,023 of 1,023 checks on the final copy, against 973 on the untouched copy. Every step's draft passes the readability check against the step before it, and plan mode checked all six again while building this page. The coding standards text injected in a Unity and Node project measures 9,496 characters against its 9,500-character budget. Not proven: the full suite run on each middle step alone (each step's own test files did pass). Also not proven: the real run in a scratch repo, which happens during the build. Another branch, issue #457 (Design loop fixes), also moves the version to 2.76.0, so whichever merges second takes the next number.
chg
Two places the rules were adjusted while drafting
Both made the check fairer without letting dense code through.

First, a name that the same block of the diff also removes already existed, so the check leaves it alone. Renaming every old name a line touches would turn small changes into rewrites, and making old code readable is issue #474 (A readable-code skill, and readable code across every repo the agent has touched). Second, short connecting words such as an, of and to are fine inside a longer name like links_an_artifact, but never as a whole name. Markdown table rows may run long, because a table cannot wrap.
choices: How should #474 (A readable-code skill) and #475 (The design loop counts every issue opened during Plan as part of the current feature) stop blocking this approval?
Label them in progress until step 5 is built
I add `in progress` to #474 (A readable-code skill) and #475 with a comment on each saying why. Once step 5 is built, your Not part of line takes them out and I remove the label.
Close both as not planned, reopen after the merge
Closing each issue needs your own message, and both stop showing as open until they are reopened.
Your approval goes through the hooks installed now, which do not have step 5's fix yet. Option A keeps both issues open and explains the label in writing; option B hides two planned pieces of work.
